question.text: Under SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, a stock broker dealing in derivatives must:

answer.text: Be registered with SEBI, meet the net-worth criteria applicable to its member category, and comply with the code of conduct
Only register with the stock exchange, not with SEBI
Have no capital requirements of any kind
Register only if dealing with institutional clients

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI registration is required for derivative brokers, dealers, and clearing members. Net-worth requirements apply by member category rather than as a single uniform stock-broker rule: a clearing member must have a net worth of Rs. 3 crore, a self-clearing member Rs. 1 crore, and both must maintain Rs. 50 lakhs of liquid net worth with the clearing corporation. SEBI has not specified a net-worth amount for trading members in the derivatives segment, leaving that criterion to the exchange. Brokers must also follow the prescribed code of conduct and the conditions attached to their registration. The Trap: Net worth is not a single all-stock-broker figure. The applicable threshold depends on whether the entity is a trading member, self-clearing member, or clearing member. Likewise, SEBI registration (not just exchange membership) is mandatory for those dealing in the derivatives segment. Note: Source basis is pp.177-181 of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives Certification Examination workbook (December 2025 v1).
